critiques.target: Noise floor (H1.1.1 tie-in; all later verdicts)
critiques.issue: The repeat run planned in I001 never happened. Every verdict since then compares a single 3-seed run against another single run. Using the per-seed sd from E001 (~0.3 pp), a 3-seed mean has sd ~0.17 pp, so the difference between two runs has sd ~0.24 pp. The 0.3 pp thresholds in H1.1.1, H2.3.1, H4.1.1 and H4.3.1 are only about 1.2 sigma. Run-to-run time noise was never measured either. E004's -0.07 s, credited to dropping cutout, is probably noise.
critiques.suggestion: Rerun E004 unchanged once (or twice) before the next verdict that depends on a difference under 0.5 pp. Record the accuracy and time deltas as the official noise floor, and restate the 'within noise' thresholds as about 2x the measured sd of a difference (likely ~0.5 pp).

critiques.issue: The only feasible run in the whole loop is E004 at 0.7550, just 0.2 pp above the 0.753 gate, from a single run. Its seed spread is 75.24 to 75.75. E006 (0.7540) is a near-replica that changes the whitening input only, which is weak evidence the recipe repeats. Still, nobody has rerun the incumbent itself. The current best time of 8.94 s also has not improved since the loop first reached feasibility; four of the five later runs were infeasible.
critiques.suggestion: Treat the E004 rerun (above) as a feasibility confirmation as well. Also log the per-seed minimum, because the 40-seed official mean needs 75.0%.

critiques.target: Description inconsistency: E004 / E005 epoch count
critiques.issue: The E004 and E005 descriptions say 'At the 8.5-epoch airbench96 recipe'. Their times (8.94 s, 9.01 s), the notebook ('at 10 ep') and E008/E009 ('Start from E004 (10 epochs…)') all point to 10 epochs. If someone read H4.1.1's +1.26 pp as an 8.5-epoch result, they would badly overestimate how many epochs can be cut.
critiques.suggestion: Correct the E004 and E005 descriptions to 10 epochs so later rewrites start from the right baseline.

critiques.issue: These carry refuting evidence (E001-, E003-, E006-) but are still 'open', and their confidence is unchanged (H1.1.1 stays at 0.55). H1.1.2's '+' is only partial: its 'crosses 0.753 between 8 and 9.5 epochs' clause is false, as the notebook itself says.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H1.1.1, H2.2.1 and H2.3.1 refuted. Split H1.1.2 into a slope claim (supported) and a crossing claim (refuted). Lower H2 to about 0.3: per E003, launch overhead is not binding, and prepare is ~0.07 s.

critiques.issue: E007 was infeasible, so it cannot support a claim about the 'best feasible' configuration being ≥10% faster. The '+' came from a pp-per-second extrapolation, and E009 then showed that extrapolation was wrong. Taken together, E007 and E009 lean toward refuting H1.2.1 for the 128/256/384 net. There is also a confound: E009 is described as a 'rewrite of I008 onto the current best recipe', which suggests E007 may have run on an older base (cutout 12 / LS 0.2?). If so, the 0.27 pp/epoch narrow-net slope in the E009 post-mortem compares two different recipes. It could also hide an odd result: the regularization change gained +1.26 pp on the wide net but almost nothing on the narrow one.
critiques.suggestion: Re-label E007 as ~ (inconclusive). Check which base E007 actually ran on. If it was the old one, the 'narrow net is capped near ~75%' conclusion rests on a confounded slope. Either run narrow at 10 ep on the E004 base, or stop citing that slope. Lower H1.2.1's confidence after E009 unless that check reverses the picture.

critiques.issue: The only measured accuracy-vs-epochs slope comes from E001→E002, under cutout 12 + LS 0.2. The notebook's own E009 lesson says slope depends on regularization and closeness to the capacity ceiling. Even so, every projection ('cash in by cutting epochs', E008's '~10.5-11 ep with resize') still uses 0.87 pp/epoch. 'Cut epochs on E004' was named as the next step after E004 and was never run.
critiques.suggestion: Run E004 at 9 or 9.5 epochs to measure the slope under the current recipe. It is cheap, it directly tests the most obvious time reduction, and every later epoch-count projection depends on it.

critiques.issue: The surprise is that progressive resizing gave the best trade seen so far, -16% time for -0.55 pp, while the committee unanimously predicted no time change. The verdict 'inconclusive' is a threshold artifact: H3.2.1 put a ≤0.3 pp accuracy bar on a lever whose real value is pp per second. The time saving (16%) is also smaller than the ~22% of FLOPs that 24 px on half the steps should save. That gap suggests the interpolate call, a recompile or graph switch, or non-conv work eats part of the benefit.
critiques.suggestion: Make the follow-up the top priority: E004 + resize at ~11 ep, plus a variant that resizes only the first 30-40% of steps. Also try downsampling once per epoch (or once in prepare) rather than per batch, and try 16 px for the earliest phase. Restate H3.2.1 as a time-at-feasibility prediction instead of an accuracy-loss bound.

critiques.issue: E004 changed two things at once: it removed cutout and lowered LS from 0.2 to 0.1. So it is unknown which change produced the +1.26 pp. The notebook says 'translate 4, LS 0.1 may still be too strong' but never tested that. This is the largest single gain in the loop, and it is the least explored afterwards.
critiques.suggestion: At 10 ep on E004, try LS 0.0 / 0.05 and translate 2 / 0, one change per run. Any gain above the measured noise floor converts directly into fewer epochs. This is probably worth more than the remaining architecture explorations.

critiques.issue: The 'supports' verdict rests on a single -0.41 pp difference, about 1.7 sigma under the estimated noise. It is directionally plausible but not established.
critiques.suggestion: Mark it E005~ or give it low weight. It needs no follow-up, because alternating flip is free and already in use, but don't cite it as a measured effect size ('~0.5 epoch worth').

critiques.issue: The E007 lesson says progress is limited by optimization steps, yet nobody tested batch size (e.g. 512 with LR scaled), which adds steps per epoch at a similar FLOP count. Only width was varied, not depth: 2 convs per block versus 3 was never tried, and neither were asymmetric widths such as 128/384/448. The LR, wd and schedule shape (H4's main claim) were never retuned. Lookahead and EMA were never ablated. H3.1 (proxy filtering) was never tried. H1.3.1 (whitening ablation) is an understanding experiment that cannot lower time.
critiques.suggestion: Add Lvl3 predictions for batch 512 at equal epochs and for 2-conv blocks at about equal time. Deprioritize or prune H1.3.1. Keep H4.2.1 (Muon) as one decisive check at most.

critiques.target: H2 throughput: compute-bound claim from E003
critiques.issue: E003 shows that launch overhead is small. That does not show the GPU is being used efficiently: ~19 ms/step for this net at batch 1024 has never been compared against A100 bf16 peak. If BN, GELU, maxpool, augmentation or the Lookahead update take a large share, there is time to save that isn't about FLOPs.
critiques.suggestion: Profile one training step (torch.profiler) and report the conv share against the elementwise/BN/optimizer share, plus a rough MFU. Also fix the ~0.08 s first-trial prepare overhead by warming the H2D path in build. It is worth ~0.027 s and costs nothing.

critiques.issue: No Lvl1 hypothesis covers what the results actually show: (a) regularization strength interacts with the epoch budget, and was the largest lever (+1.26 pp, ~1.4 epochs); (b) the accuracy-vs-epochs slope depends on the architecture's capacity ceiling (E009); (c) resolution is a FLOP lever with a favourable accuracy cost (E008). H1 treats epochs × FLOPs/epoch as separable, and E009 contradicts that. H2 is largely spent.
critiques.suggestion: Add a Lvl1 along these lines: 'time-to-75% is set by the per-FLOP learning rate of the recipe, where regularization strength, resolution schedule and capacity jointly determine the slope and ceiling'. Move H3.2 and H4.1 under it as mechanisms, and demote H2.

structured_output.summary: Only one run is feasible so far: E004 (0.7550, 8.94 s), from a single run with a 0.2 pp margin. The noise floor was never measured, so verdicts on differences under ~0.5 pp, such as E005 (-0.41 pp), are statistically weak. The bookkeeping is stale: H1.1.1, H2.2.1 and H2.3.1 have been refuted but are still 'open'. H1.2.1's E007+ came from an infeasible run and is contradicted by E009, which may itself be confounded if E007 used an older recipe. The E004/E005 descriptions say 8.5 epochs, but the runs were actually 10. Every epoch projection still uses a slope measured under the old heavy-regularization recipe, and the obvious 'cut epochs on E004' run was never done. The real surprise is E008: progressive resizing gave -16% time for -0.55 pp, the best trade so far, and nobody predicted it. Its 'inconclusive' label is just a threshold artifact. Suggested order: (1) rerun E004 to get the noise floor and confirm feasibility; (2) E004 + resize at ~11 ep, plus shorter low-res phases; (3) push regularization further (LS 0–0.05, translate 0–2), one change at a time; (4) E004 at 9–9.5 ep to measure the current slope; (5) batch 512, depth variants, and a step profile. Restructure the tree around regularization × resolution × capacity as what sets the accuracy-per-FLOP curve, and demote H2.
